dokimasia-closure-m.claim: The covered state is driven against an oracle nobody has acted on and must refuse, so a closure ratio cannot be reached by citing cases that were never run.

dokimasia-closure-o.claim: The nearest overclaim is inferred coverage: with no disposition declared, the reconciler must report none covered rather than matching the two sides itself.

dokimasia-closure-s.claim: Two dispositions on one item are refused, so nothing can be recorded as both decided and undecided.

dokimasia-inventory-m.claim: Each declared path rule and cap is driven against a tree that breaches it and must refuse by name, so a cap that never fires cannot pass as a guarantee.

dokimasia-inventory-p.claim: Positive evidence compiles the committed fixture and requires the record to carry exactly the keys the inventory schema declares.

dokimasia-inventory-r.claim: Recovery evidence requires the refusal to name the cap and the path that breached it, so the caller can correct the input rather than guess.

dokimasia-inventory-s.claim: A compile whose two runs disagree is refused, so a digest cannot be recorded against a tree that does not reproduce.

dokimasia-propose-m.claim: The misuse driven is drafting the one state ADR-001 reserves to a person: the executable source is required to carry no covered literal and the draftable pair is asserted, so the absence is a property of the code rather than a filter that could be removed.

dokimasia-propose-o.claim: The boundary on what a draft establishes is asserted directly: a complete drafted set answers for nothing until a person confirms it, so drafting cannot move a coverage figure.

dokimasia-propose-p.claim: Positive evidence drafts an entry for every scoped item exactly once, so the reviewer is handed a complete set rather than a partial one they must finish by hand.

dokimasia-propose-r.claim: Recovery evidence requires a set answering for one item twice to refuse by naming the item, so the caller repairs the duplicate rather than the generator picking a copy.

dokimasia-propose-s.claim: The declared write boundary is driven with a label carrying a separator and parent references, which must refuse and leave nothing outside the evidence root.

dokimasia-scaffold-m.claim: A mutated copy of the root law makes the same byte comparison fail, so the installed-copy check refuses drift instead of passing trivially.

dokimasia-scaffold-o.claim: The nearest overclaim is a verb that answers with coverage: every unbuilt verb is required to leave standard output empty, so no caller can read a closure ratio off this version.

dokimasia-scaffold-s.claim: A contract left at a superseded version is refused, so a stale declaration cannot ride along beside a moved manifest.

dokimasia-scrutiny-o.claim: The nearest overclaim is a target reported as an observation: the recorded duration must be measured and must not equal the declared budget.

synkrisis-cohort-m.claim: A missing or failed upstream validation result is refused rather than treated as success.

synkrisis-cohort-o.claim: The nearest tempting overclaim, an unknown observer counted as data, remains unavailable.

synkrisis-cohort-p.claim: Positive evidence exercises cohort construction inside its declared boundary.

synkrisis-cohort-r.claim: A refusal names its recovery and the repaired declared universe reruns clean.

synkrisis-cohort-s.claim: Replaced record bytes are refused against the declared digest rather than silently reread.

synkrisis-diagnose-m.claim: A rule whose minimum sample counts are not met is refused visibly rather than matched thinly.

synkrisis-diagnose-o.claim: Findings stay at the inferred evidence class; the stronger classes remain unavailable.

synkrisis-diagnose-p.claim: Positive evidence recomputes both shipped rule kinds from the checked example cohort.

synkrisis-diagnose-r.claim: A refused catalogue reruns clean after the named rule is repaired.

synkrisis-diagnose-s.claim: A record changed after cohort construction is refused against the cohort's digests.

synkrisis-verify-m.claim: A missing artefact is refused rather than reported as verified.

synkrisis-verify-o.claim: Verification emits digests and one status; it never blesses the suggested handoff.

synkrisis-verify-p.claim: Positive evidence recomputes cohort, findings and report byte for byte from the original inputs.

synkrisis-verify-r.claim: Verification reruns clean after the named artefact is restored.

synkrisis-verify-s.claim: A stale rule digest is refused rather than verified against newer rules.

tabularium-m.claim: Missing required evidence is refused rather than treated as success.

tabularium-o.claim: The nearest tempting overclaim remains explicitly unavailable.

tabularium-p.claim: Positive evidence exercises the declared operation inside its stated boundary.

tabularium-r.claim: The failure is contained and leaves a concrete rerun, rollback or repair path.

tabularium-s.claim: Stale or mismatched subject evidence is refused or kept visibly scoped.

vulgate-eval-m.claim: The labelled case refuses a rewrite with no exact source or parity comparison.

vulgate-eval-o.claim: The labelled case keeps register rewriting narrower than truth, authorship or argument improvement.

vulgate-eval-p.claim: The labelled positive case supports an inferred content-parity judgement without claiming truth.

vulgate-eval-r.claim: The labelled recovery restores lost content and repeats the complete comparison.

vulgate-eval-s.claim: The labelled case refuses source bytes from a different draft.
